summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a homeless man with chronic systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and alcohol use disorder, was admitted for chest pain and alcohol intoxication. He exhibited mild alcohol withdrawal symptoms, which resolved with minimal benzodiazepine use and supportive care. His chest pain was determined to be non-cardiac, likely due to cervical spine degenerative changes affecting nerve roots, and was managed with gabapentin and a lidocaine patch. A CT scan incidentally revealed right lower lobe pneumonia, which was improving clinically and radiologically, requiring no further antibiotics. His chronic conditions, including pulmonary embolism, were stabilized with continued enoxaparin, heart failure medications, and B12 supplementation. He remained compliant with anticoagulation and was discharged home to a shelter with instructions to follow up with his primary care provider and psychiatry for ongoing management of substance use, depression, and cardiac health.
